Full details: Linked Issues check
**Explanation** Issue `#2773` requires that a request body containing \u0000 is saved, not replaced by {"message":"invalid text"}. The diff adds stripJSONNul in internal/server/biz/request.go and applies it to the database-bound bytes in CreateRequest and CreateRequestExecution (request bodies). Before the change, PostgreSQL jsonb rejected these bytes (SQLSTATE 22P05), so the placeholder retry ran. After the change, the NUL escape is removed before Save, so the jsonb write succeeds and the original content is kept minus the NUL. This matches the issue's suggested fix (strip NUL before storage). The four response-body writes (UpdateRequestFinalized, UpdateRequestCompletedWithAudio, UpdateRequestStatusExternalIDAndResponseBody, UpdateRequestExecutionFinalized) also use stripJSONNul, so a NUL in a response no longer fails the status update. TestStripJSONNul in request_nul_test.go covers no NUL, single and multiple NULs, \\u0000 (kept), \\\u0000 (NUL removed), and other \uXXXX escapes (kept). Not implemented, by design per the PR description: the UI notice and the explicit failure marker for the case where a body cannot be saved (issue Expected Behavior, second clause), and changes to the external-storage error path (issue suggestion 3). The second clause applies only when saving is impossible. With NUL removed, the NUL case no longer reaches that branch. The placeholder fallback still exists for other save errors, which the issue does not describe. Read-side restoration is not requested by the issue.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check
**Explanation** All changes in the diff serve the NUL-escape fix. stripJSONNul is a new helper in request.go. Its call sites are the database-bound request-body and response-body writes that receive the same jsonb rejection. External-storage payloads and markers are unchanged, as the PR states. The new test file request_nul_test.go tests only stripJSONNul. The diff adds no imports, so the bytes package used by bytes.Contains and bytes.HasPrefix is already present. No unrelated refactoring or behavior change appears in the diff. Extending the fix to response bodies is connected to the issue: it uses the same jsonb column and the same SQLSTATE 22P05 failure, and the PR summary identifies it as part of the same root cause.
